It uses standard AUR packaging practices: fetching source via `git+https`, skipping checksums (which is expected and acceptable for VCS sources), and invoking an upstream `install.sh` script to build and install the theme variants.

The `install.sh` script is executed in a controlled manner, with predictable arguments to generate different theme variants (e.g., compact, black, nord). This script is part of the upstream source and its use is consistent with the theme's documented installation method. No network calls, file operations outside the package directory, or suspicious commands (e.g., `curl | bash`, `eval`, obfuscated payloads) are present. All operations are confined to `$srcdir` and `$pkgdir`, as expected in a safe PKGBUILD.

While the use of an upstream shell script (`install.sh`) inherently carries some risk if that script were malicious, this is not a supply-chain compromise of the AUR package itself. The package does not inject code or modify the upstream behavior. The risk, if any, lies with the upstream project, which is outside the scope of this AUR package audit.
</details>
